investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs at this time. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 (createAgent call) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads, leaving zero allocatable units for new pods. [Possible] A node that previously carried kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or lost its extended-resource advertisement (e.g., device plugin crash or node restart), reducing effective capacity below what the eval workload requires.

[Possible but unproven] A burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) may have saturated the 2 eligible nodes simultaneously, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs at this time. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 (createAgent call) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-08-04 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~134–152 s), preventing agent creation and causing all downstream eval checks to fail with empty evidence. This is a cluster-infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is currently scoped to these observability evals.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 affinity-matching nodes — no capacity remains for new peer-pod VMs, and preemption found no evictable victims. All three checks failed with this exact message.

[Secondary] The 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector (e.g., a node label, taint, or topology constraint required for kata peer-pods), reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity exhaustion.

[Less likely] A prior eval run or external workload left orphaned kata peer-pod VMs running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming the vm quota without releasing it — the withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) may not have completed cleanup if a previous run was interrupted.

[Least likely / no current evidence] A cluster configuration change (node label removal, resource quota reduction, or affinity rule tightening) reduced the schedulable surface; no suspect changes are listed in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.
